sessions.title: Session #1: Full-Spectrum Staff SDET Synthesis — Distributed Systems, CDP, RAG & DORA (Final Boss)

questions.title: Q1: 50-Worker Distributed Test Data Isolation & Kafka Eventual Consistency
questions.scenario: 30+ microservices with Kafka/Debezium suffer 50-worker staging collisions and async assertion races.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Use cryptographic X-Test-Tenant-ID / UUID entity partitioning + domain Test Data Builders; verify Kafka sagas via correlation-ID consumer harnesses or bounded exponential-backoff polling (never Thread.sleep); guarantee SIGKILL cleanup via TTL-tagged rows and an out-of-band Reaper cron + Saga compensation.

questions.title: Q2: Playwright CDP WebSockets vs Selenium W3C HTTP & BrowserContext Memory
questions.scenario: Migrating 10,000 Java Selenium tests to Playwright across 32-thread Kubernetes pods.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Selenium serializes each command over HTTP REST roundtrips and spawns heavy OS browsers per thread (~500MB RAM), whereas Playwright multiplexes JSON-RPC over a persistent CDP WebSocket and isolates 32 workers via lightweight BrowserContexts (~20MB, <20ms startup). Mitigate SSR hydration races with getByRole accessibility locators + API response waits.

questions.title: Q3: Enterprise RAG Triad Evaluation Gate & AST Self-Healing Locator Agent
questions.scenario: Gating an airline policy RAG concierge against hallucinations and building a safe self-healing UI agent.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Decompose RAG into Faithfulness (supported claims / total claims), Answer Relevance, and Context Recall/Precision over a stratified golden dataset with strict CI thresholds (>=0.90). For self-healing, snapshot DOM + Accessibility Tree, require high role+embedding confidence + state-transition verification, and emit an AST-patched PR rather than mutating main.

questions.title: Q4: OpenTelemetry W3C TraceContext Propagation & Automated 504 RCA Triage
questions.scenario: Pinpointing staging 504/500 spikes across 30 K8s microservices, Kong gateway, Kafka, and Stripe.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Inject W3C `traceparent` headers in API test clients and assert propagation across HTTP -> Kafka headers -> worker spans. Distinguish external gateway latency (long leaf client span) vs DB pool starvation (wait-acquire span spike) vs K8s CFS throttling (`container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total`), and auto-query traces on test failure to post structured RCA.

questions.title: Q5: Compressing 1,500 Machine-Hour Regression, Flake Quarantine & DORA
questions.scenario: Overhauling an 8,000-test, 14-hour, 16%-flaky E2E suite blocking daily releases.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Shift 70% of E2E combinatorial checks down into Pact consumer-driven contracts + component tests, apply Git-diff Test Impact Analysis (TIA) + LPT duration bin-packing across K8s shards, auto-quarantine statistically flaky tests into non-blocking jobs with strict CODEOWNERS repair SLAs, and tie outcomes directly to the 4 DORA metrics.

sessions.title: Session #2: Frontend & Browser Architecture — CDP Pipes, Context Memory & Hydration (Phase 1 Exit Gate)

questions.title: Q1: Flakiness Combinatorics (p^N) & Hermetic UI Seam Economics
questions.scenario: A checkout SPA suite has 250 browser tests each passing 99.2% of runs independently, yet PR builds fail over 85% of the time.
tasks: Prove mathematically why 99.2% per-test reliability collapses across 250 tests (`P = p^N`) and calculate the per-test reliability needed for 95% green CI runs.
Design a Hermetic UI Seam strategy deciding what runs against real backend pods vs deterministic network route mocks (`page.route` / HAR).
Explain why blind `@Retry(3)` hides concurrency bugs and inflates CI cost.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: `0.992^250 = 0.134` (86.6% build failure!). Reaching `0.95` across 250 tests requires `p = 0.95^(1/250) = 0.99979`. Keep 10–15 true E2E smoke journeys unmocked while shifting 235 UI state permutations onto OpenAPI/Pact-verified `page.route` seams rather than masking races with blind `@Retry`.

questions.title: Q2: Browser Process vs BrowserContext Memory Sizing on K8s Runners
questions.scenario: Your Playwright runner pods (`4 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM`, `/dev/shm` default `64 MiB`) crash with `Target closed` and Exit Code `137` at 16 workers.
tasks: Calculate memory footprint comparing 16 OS Chromium processes vs 1 Browser + 16 isolated `BrowserContext` instances.
Diagnose why Docker's `64 MiB` `/dev/shm` crashes Chromium compositors and specify exact container flags/mounts.
Design zero-UI authentication state reuse (`storageState`) across 16 parallel worker personas without session token collisions.
antiPatterns: login via ui before every test
share one mutable user across workers
questions.benchmarkAnswer: 1 Browser (~350MB) + 16 BrowserContexts (16 * 25MB = 400MB) fits comfortably under 1.5 GiB vs 8+ GiB for 16 full browsers. Mount tmpfs `/dev/shm` >= 1–2 GiB (or `--disable-dev-shm-usage`) to prevent Exit 137 SIGKILL, and mint per-worker API `storageState` JSONs in setup so workers skip UI login with zero cart collisions.

questions.title: Q3: Next.js SSR Hydration Races, Shadow DOM & Five Actionability Gates
questions.scenario: Tests click a visible server-rendered `Book Seat` button in Next.js, Playwright reports `click()` succeeded, yet no `/api/orders` POST fires.
tasks: List Playwright's 5 Actionability Gates and explain why SSR hydration still defeats them.
Architect a deterministic fix across app instrumentation (`data-hydrated` / readiness signals) and web-first assertions.
Explain how closed vs open Shadow DOM piercing and cross-origin payment `iframe` (`Stripe Elements`) locators work.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Playwright verifies Attached, Visible, Stable, Receives Events, and Enabled—but SSR paints enabled HTML before React attaches JS `onClick` handlers. Emit deterministic hydration readiness (`data-hydrated='true'`) or assert post-hydration interactive state, use CSS/getByRole auto-piercing on open Shadow roots, and isolate Stripe iframes via `page.frameLocator()`.

questions.title: Q4: Deterministic Clock Virtualization, WebSocket Mocking & Network Faults
questions.scenario: AeroCart's seat-hold countdown expires after 10 minutes over a live WebSocket ticker and shows a degraded banner on HTTP 429/503.
tasks: Design a sub-second test verifying the 10-minute countdown expiry without waiting 600 real seconds (`page.clock`).
Architect deterministic WebSocket frame interception (`page.routeWebSocket`) for concurrent seat-snatch events.
Test UI retry/degradation banners under injected `429 Retry-After` and `503` upstream faults.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Install `page.clock.install()` before navigation and call `clock.fastForward('10:01')` to trigger expiry in <50ms. Use `page.routeWebSocket()` to inject synthetic `SEAT_LOCKED` frames deterministically, and `page.route('**/api/v1/orders')` returning `429` with `Retry-After: 2` to assert accessible `role='alert'` degradation banners.

questions.title: Q5: Visual Pixel-Diffing vs Accessibility (`axe-core`) Gates & Blob Sharding
questions.scenario: Font anti-aliasing differences between macOS laptops and Linux CI runners break `toHaveScreenshot()` on every PR.
tasks: Solve cross-OS font/GPU rendering drift so visual regression tests stay 100% reproducible.
Define WCAG 2.1 AA automated gates (`@axe-core/playwright`) and what human/screen-reader gaps remain.
Design sharded Playwright execution merging Blob reports (`--reporter=blob` -> `merge-reports`).
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Generate and verify visual baselines exclusively inside pinned Linux Playwright Docker images, masking dynamic timestamps/avatars and disabling CSS animations. Pair `@axe-core/playwright` WCAG 2.1 AA checks (4.5:1 contrast, labels, focus traps) with keyboard tab-order tests, and aggregate `--shard=i/N` runs via `playwright merge-reports`.

sessions.title: Session #3: Microservices, Async Kafka & Flake Governance — Pact, Outbox & Quarantine (Phase 2 Exit Gate)

questions.title: Q1: Consumer-Driven Pact Contracts vs OpenAPI Schema Validation
questions.scenario: 35 teams deploy independently; OpenAPI linters pass, yet Checkout breaks when Pricing renames an optional nested enum.
tasks: Contrast provider-side OpenAPI schema validation against Consumer-Driven Contracts (Pact Broker + `can-i-deploy`).
Handle Provider States (`given('Flight AC-101 has 2 seats left')`) deterministically without shared staging DBs.
Contract-test asynchronous Kafka / Avro / Protobuf event schemas (`BACKWARD` vs `FULL` compatibility).
antiPatterns: test all 35 services only in shared staging
questions.benchmarkAnswer: OpenAPI proves syntactic validity on the provider, whereas Pact records exact consumer field/value expectations and gates releases via Pact Broker `can-i-deploy` verification matrices. Seed in-memory/transactional Provider State handlers per interaction and enforce Schema Registry `BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE`/`FULL` rules on Kafka topics.

questions.title: Q2: Transactional Outbox, Debezium CDC & Idempotent Payment Sagas
questions.scenario: Network blips during `POST /orders` cause duplicate credit-card charges OR DB commits whose `OrderCreated` Kafka event is lost.
tasks: Explain the Dual-Write bug (Postgres commit + Kafka publish) and verify the Transactional Outbox + Debezium CDC fix.
Design automated chaos tests proving `Idempotency-Key` safety under concurrent duplicate POST retries.
Test multi-step Saga compensation when Inventory reservation fails after Payment pre-auth succeeds.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Eliminate dual-writes by inserting `orders` + `outbox_events` in one local ACID transaction streamed via Debezium WAL CDC, with consumer deduplication on `event_id`. Fire 16 concurrent barrier-synchronized `POST /orders` sharing one `Idempotency-Key` asserting exactly 1 ledger charge, and inject Inventory `503` to assert Payment void/compensation.

questions.title: Q3: HTTP/2 Connection Pooling, Token-Bucket Rate Limiting & Full-Jitter Backoff
questions.scenario: During flash-sale tests, retry storms amplify a 2-second downstream hiccup into a 20-minute cascading outage.
tasks: Explain retry amplification across 4 microservice hops and prove why Exponential Backoff + **Full Jitter** beats fixed intervals.
Verify Token-Bucket rate limiters (`capacity`, `refill_rate`, `429 Retry-After`) without wall-clock sleeps.
Prevent client-side retry budgets from exhausting HTTP connection pools.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: 3 retries across 4 hops multiplies load `4^4 = 256x`! Randomize sleep `uniform(0, min(cap, base * 2^attempt))` (Full Jitter) to desynchronize waves, cap per-client retry budgets at <=10% of active requests + propagate deadlines, and test Token Bucket math deterministically via an injected monotonic clock.

questions.title: Q4: GraphQL N+1 Query Traps & gRPC Protobuf Deadline / Status Contracts
questions.scenario: An API gateway exposes GraphQL to web/mobile and talks gRPC internally; nested `flights { crew {certs} }` queries spike DB load 100x.
tasks: Detect and fail GraphQL `N+1` resolver regressions automatically inside integration CI.
Test GraphQL AST depth/cost limits and partial-data `errors[]` envelopes (`HTTP 200` trap!).
Verify gRPC deadline propagation (`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`), wire-compatibility (field tags), and status codes.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Instrument SQL/OTel span counters in GraphQL tests asserting query count stays `O(1)` (`<= 3` batched DataLoader queries whether returning 2 or 50 flights), assert `response.errors` is empty (since GraphQL returns HTTP 200 on resolver errors) + AST query-depth caps, and lint Protobuf `reserved` field tags with `buf breaking`.

questions.title: Q5: Statistical Flake Detection (Beta-Binomial / Rolling Pass Rate) & Quarantine Governance
questions.scenario: Engineers re-run red GitHub Actions jobs until green; 12% of tests are intermittent flakes with zero accountability.
tasks: Define an objective statistical flake detector distinguishing true code regressions from non-deterministic tests.
Architect automated quarantine routing (blocking PR lane vs non-blocking quarantine lane) via JUnit/Allure telemetry.
Enforce CODEOWNERS SLAs and strict un-quarantine graduation gates (e.g., 100 consecutive parallel burn-in passes).
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Flag any test exhibiting mixed pass+fail outcomes on the *exact same commit SHA* (or >1% retry rate over 200 runs), auto-move it via quarantine manifest out of blocking PR checks into a monitored quarantine pipeline, page CODEOWNERS with a 7-day fix-or-rewrite SLA, and require 100/100 parallel stress burn-in passes to re-enter the PR gate.

sessions.title: Session #4: SQL Data Integrity, Containers & CI Sharding — MVCC, Ryuk & LPT (Phase 3 Exit Gate)
sessions.shortTitle: Session #4: SQL MVCC, Docker & LPT Sharding
sessions.targetRole: Staff Data, Infrastructure & CI Systems Architect

questions.title: Q1: PostgreSQL MVCC Isolation Anomaly & 64-Thread Seat `12A` Double-Booking
questions.scenario: Under `READ COMMITTED`, `SELECT available FROM seats WHERE seat='12A'` followed by `UPDATE` double-books Seat `12A` under 64 concurrent requests.
tasks: Explain why PostgreSQL `READ COMMITTED` permits Lost Updates / Read-Modify-Write races across concurrent transactions.
Compare Pessimistic Locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` vs `SKIP LOCKED`), Optimistic CAS (`version = version + 1`), and `SERIALIZABLE` SSI.
Write the concurrency test harness (cyclic barrier + 64 threads) proving exactly 1 winner and 63 clean `409 Conflict` responses.
antiPatterns: synchronize in python memory across multiple pods
questions.benchmarkAnswer: In `READ COMMITTED`, two transactions both read `available=true` from the committed snapshot before either commits. Use `UPDATE seats SET booked_by=:u, version=version+1 WHERE seat='12A' AND booked_by IS NULL` (atomic single-statement CAS) for named seats or `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for next-available seat queues, verified via a 64-thread `threading.Barrier` test.

questions.title: Q2: 1:N Join Fan-Out Financial Inflation & Double-Entry Ledger Reconciliation
questions.scenario: Joining `orders` (`1` row, `$500`) to `baggage_items` (`3` rows) and `tax_lines` (`2` rows) inflates `SUM(orders.total_cents)` to `$3,000` (`6x`!).
tasks: Explain the Cartesian `1:M:N` join grain trap and rewrite the SQL using pre-aggregated CTEs.
Enforce double-entry ledger invariants (`SUM(debits) == SUM(credits)`, zero orphan journal postings, idempotent webhook replay).
Verify query scalability via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` SARGable composite B-Tree indexes.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Never sum parent metrics after joining `1:N` child tables (`3 * 2 = 6x` row multiplication); pre-aggregate each child table to `order_id` grain inside separate CTEs before joining, store money in integer cents/NUMERIC with `SUM(debit_cents) - SUM(credit_cents) = 0` checks, and assert `Index Only Scan` / zero `Seq Scan` via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`.

questions.title: Q3: Multi-Stage Dockerfiles, BuildKit Layer Caching & Testcontainers Ryuk Reaper
questions.scenario: Your E2E runner Docker image is `2.9 GB`, rebuilds `pip/maven` from scratch on every 1-line test edit (`9 min`), and leaks zombie Postgres containers on CI.
tasks: Redesign a Multi-Stage BuildKit Dockerfile cutting image size >65% and keeping dependency layers cached across code edits.
Harden container security (non-root `USER`, pinned digests, zero build-arg secrets in image history).
Explain how Testcontainers `Ryuk` sidecar reaps orphan containers/volumes even when CI runners receive `SIGKILL`.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Copy lockfiles (`pyproject.toml`/`pom.xml`) and install dependencies with `--mount=type=cache` *before* `COPY . .`, copy artifacts into a minimal runtime stage running as non-root `USER 10001` (using Debian-slim/glibc for Playwright browser compatibility), and keep Testcontainers' `Ryuk` TCP heartbeat sidecar enabled to garbage-collect labeled containers/networks on socket disconnect.

questions.title: Q4: Kubernetes Ephemeral PR Environments, Probes & `OOMKilled (Exit 137)` Forensics
questions.scenario: Ephemeral PR namespaces suffer sporadic `502 Bad Gateway` during rollout and test pods die with `Exit Code 137` despite JVM `-Xmx6g` on an `8Gi` pod.
tasks: Explain why `-Xmx6g` inside an `8Gi` cgroup v2 pod still triggers Linux OOMKiller (`Exit 137`).
Differentiate Kubernetes `startupProbe`, `readinessProbe`, and `livenessProbe` to eliminate rollout `502`s and restart loops.
Design graceful `SIGTERM` connection draining (`preStop` + `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`).
antiPatterns: put downstream db check inside livenessProbe
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Total pod RSS = Heap (`6Gi`) + Metaspace + Thread stacks + Direct NIO buffers + glibc arenas + Chromium/native sidecars (>8Gi -> cgroup OOMKill 137); cap JVM at `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70.0`. Never check downstream DBs in `livenessProbe` (causes cascading restarts); gate traffic with `readinessProbe` + `preStop` sleep so kube-proxy updates Endpoints before `SIGTERM`.

questions.title: Q5: Longest-Processing-Time (LPT) CI Shard Bin-Packing & AST Test Impact Analysis
questions.scenario: Alphabetical sharding puts all slow Checkout E2E specs onto Shard #3 (`28 min`) while Shards #1, #2, and #4 finish in `5 min`.
tasks: Write/explain the `O(N log K)` Longest-Processing-Time (LPT) Min-Heap bin-packing algorithm using historical p90 test durations.
Calculate wall-clock speedup and machine-minute savings across `K = 8` shards.
Combine static AST import-graph + coverage Test Impact Analysis (TIA) on PRs with full nightly safety nets.
antiPatterns: never run full suite on main/nightly
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Sort test files descending by rolling p90 duration and greedily assign each file to the lightest shard via a `K`-element Min-Heap (`O(N log K)`, proven `<= 4/3 - 1/(3K)` optimal makespan), collapsing 28m skew down to balanced ~10m shards. Pair AST/coverage TIA on PRs with mandatory full runs when shared config/Dockerfile/fixtures change.

sessions.title: Session #5: Performance, Chaos SRE & App/AI Security — Little's Law, SLOs & Zero-Trust (Phase 4 Exit Gate)
sessions.targetRole: Staff Performance, Chaos & Security QE Architect

questions.title: Q1: Little's Law (`L = λW`), Connection Pool Sizing & Coordinated Omission
questions.scenario: A closed-loop 50-VU load test reports `p99 = 45ms`, yet production users hit `4.2s` freezes during 1.5-second JVM/DB pauses at `500 RPS`.
tasks: Explain **Coordinated Omission** in closed-loop VUs vs open-loop constant-arrival-rate schedules (`k6` / `HdrHistogram`).
Apply Little's Law (`L = λ * W`) at `λ = 500 RPS` during a `W = 400ms` downstream slowdown to size thread & HikariCP DB pools without thrashing.
Design load-shedding / queue-timeout bounds before pool starvation cascades.
antiPatterns: set db pool size to 2000 per pod
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Closed-loop VUs wait for a stalled request before firing the next, measuring only 1 slow sample instead of the 750 requests queued behind a 1.5s stall (Coordinated Omission)—use open-loop constant-arrival executors. By Little's Law, `500 RPS * 0.4s = 200` concurrent in-flight requests, while DB connections per Postgres core stay bounded (`~2 * cores + spindle`) via async I/O + fast `503` load shedding.

questions.title: Q2: Scientific Chaos Engineering (`Toxiproxy`), Circuit Breakers & Soak Leak Detection
questions.scenario: Injecting a Redis timeout in staging brings down Flight Search completely instead of falling back cleanly.
tasks: Structure a scientific Chaos Experiment (Steady-State Hypothesis, Blast-Radius Abort Condition, Toxiproxy toxic injection).
Verify 3-state Circuit Breaker transitions (`CLOSED -> OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED`) and Bulkhead isolation.
Detect slow off-heap memory / file-descriptor (`FD`) leaks in a 6-hour soak test using linear regression slope gates.
antiPatterns: kill random prod nodes without steady-state metrics
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Define quantitative steady-state SLIs first, inject deterministic TCP latency/reset via Toxiproxy on the Redis upstream, and assert the Circuit Breaker trips `OPEN` within threshold—serving degraded uncached search (`200 OK`) inside an isolated thread/semaphore Bulkhead. Gate soak runs on post-GC RSS and open-FD slope (`~0 MB/hr` after warmup).

questions.title: Q3: Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate SLO Gates (`14.4x` / `6x`) & Canary Rollbacks
questions.scenario: Static `> 1% error rate for 5m` alerts page engineers on harmless blips yet miss slow 3-day error-budget exhaustion.
tasks: Calculate the monthly 30-day Error Budget for a `99.9%` availability SLO (`43.2 minutes` / `0.1%` bad requests).
Explain Google SRE Multi-Window Multi-Burn-Rate alerts (`1h/5m` at `14.4x` fast burn vs `6h/30m` at `6x` burn).
Automate Canary deployment rollback gates comparing canary vs baseline pods statistically (Mann-Whitney / error ratio).
antiPatterns: compare canary against last week instead of live baseline
questions.benchmarkAnswer: A `99.9%` 30-day SLO grants `0.1%` error budget (`43.2 min`). A `14.4x` burn consumes `2%` of the monthly budget in `1 hour` (paired with a `5m` short window so alerts clear immediately once mitigated), while `6x` catches `5%` burn over `6h/30m`. Compare canary pods side-by-side against simultaneous baseline pods to avoid diurnal traffic bias.

questions.title: Q4: Automated OWASP API Security — BOLA (`IDOR`), Mass Assignment & RFC 8725 JWT
questions.scenario: A user swaps `/api/v1/orders/ORD-99` with Tenant A's valid JWT and reads Tenant B's passport details (`200 OK`).
tasks: Build an automated Cross-Tenant BOLA/BFLA matrix test harness running on every OpenAPI endpoint.
Test RFC 8725 JWT attacks (`alg: none`, RS256->HS256 public-key confusion, unverified `kid` injection, missing `aud`/`exp`).
Catch Mass Assignment (`role: 'admin'`, `price_cents: 0`) via strict DTO allowlisting tests.
antiPatterns: check authn middleware without object-level owner check
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Provision Alice (`Tenant A`) and Bob (`Tenant B`) fixtures and replay Alice's resource IDs across `GET/PUT/DELETE` using Bob's valid JWT asserting `403/404` (never `200`). Fuzz JWT headers for `alg:none`, RS256->HS256 key confusion, and expired/wrong-`aud` claims while enforcing server-side algorithm pinning, and assert `extra='forbid'` DTOs reject injected privilege/price fields.

questions.title: Q5: Cloud Metadata SSRF (`169.254.169.254` / IMDSv2), Webhook HMAC Replay & Race-Condition Double-Spend
questions.scenario: An invoice-logo URL previewer fetches user-supplied URLs, and a Stripe refund webhook lacks timestamp replay protection.
tasks: Prevent SSRF against cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`, IPv6/octal bypasses, DNS rebinding) + enforce AWS IMDSv2 hop-limit.
Verify Webhook authenticity (`HMAC-SHA256` constant-time `hmac.compare_digest` + `5-minute` timestamp replay window).
Write a parallel Race-Condition Double-Spend security test (`20` simultaneous coupon/wallet redemptions).
antiPatterns: blacklist string '169.254' only before dns resolution
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Resolve DNS once in a custom socket dialer and block RFC1918/link-local/loopback IPs (`169.254.0.0/16`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `10.0.0.0/8`) with redirects disabled + AWS IMDSv2 `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1`. Verify webhooks over raw body bytes using `hmac.compare_digest` + `<=300s` timestamp skew + nonce cache, and fire 20 barrier-synced redemptions asserting balance never goes negative.

sessions.title: Session #6: Production AI Engineering & Agentic QE — Hybrid RRF, Judge Calibration & MCP Agents (Phase 5 Exit Gate)
sessions.shortTitle: Session #6: Production AI, RAG & Agentic QE
sessions.targetRole: Staff AI Quality & LLM Evaluation Systems Architect

questions.title: Q1: Hybrid BM25 + HNSW Vector Retrieval, RRF Math & Cross-Encoder Reranking
questions.scenario: Dense embeddings alone miss exact flight numbers (`AC-409`, `EU-261`) and chunking mid-table splits fee amounts from cabin headers.
tasks: Architect structure-aware chunking + Contextual Retrieval + Hybrid BM25 + HNSW fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (`k=60`).
Explain why two-stage Bi-Encoder top-50 -> Cross-Encoder top-5 reranking improves precision while keeping p95 latency < 150ms.
Measure offline retrieval quality (`Recall@K`, `MRR`, `NDCG@K`) before touching LLM prompts.
antiPatterns: naive fixed 500-char split cutting markdown tables
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Keep Markdown/HTML tables intact with prepended document/section headers (Contextual Retrieval), fuse Okapi BM25 + HNSW dense hits via scale-invariant RRF `sum(1 / (60 + rank))`, rerank top-50 candidates to top-5 with a Cross-Encoder (`<80ms`), and gate index changes on `Recall@5` and `NDCG@5`.

questions.title: Q2: LLM-as-a-Judge Bias Modes & Rogan-Gladen Prevalence Calibration
questions.scenario: Your GPT/Gemini judge reports `84%` pass-rate, exhibits verbosity & position bias in A/B comparisons, and drifts across judge versions.
tasks: Derive and apply **Rogan-Gladen** prevalence calibration (`p_hat = (p_obs + q0 - 1) / (q1 + q0 - 1)`) using a human-labeled gold audit set.
Mitigate pairwise position bias, verbosity bias, and self-preference bias in automated evals.
Compute bootstrap 95% confidence intervals so noisy 2% swings don't trigger false CI blocks.
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Calibrate binary atomic rubrics (`temperature=0`) against a 200-sample human gold set (`Cohen's kappa >= 0.75`) to measure judge `TPR (q1)` and `TNR (q0)`, debiasing raw `p_obs` via `p_hat = clip((p_obs + q0 - 1)/(q1 + q0 - 1), 0, 1)` with bootstrap 95% CIs, and run A/B pairwise evals in both `(A,B)` and `(B,A)` orders.

questions.title: Q3: Negation Flips, Numeric Hallucinations & Abstention (`IDK`) Metamorphic QA
questions.scenario: An airline bot passes cosine-similarity checks even when it says `'Economy tickets ARE refundable after 24h'` (policy says `'NOT refundable'`).
tasks: Explain why embedding cosine similarity fails catastrophically on negation flips, numeric swaps (`$75` vs `$750`), and entity swaps.
Design claim-decomposition NLI entailment + deterministic numeric/policy-rule extractors.
Build Metamorphic & Unanswerable-Query (`Abstention`) tests verifying the bot refuses out-of-scope legal/competitor questions.
antiPatterns: grade rag answers using only embedding cosine similarity
questions.benchmarkAnswer: `'Tickets are refundable'` and `'Tickets are NOT refundable'` share >0.96 cosine similarity! Decompose answers into atomic claims verified by 3-way NLI (`ENTAILMENT / NEUTRAL / CONTRADICTION`) + exact regex number/currency subset checks against cited chunks, and maintain an unanswerable/perturbed metamorphic suite asserting clean abstention.

questions.title: Q4: Multi-Turn MCP Tool-Calling Agent QA, Replay Cassettes & Indirect Prompt Injection
questions.scenario: A customer-support MCP agent can read emails/policies and call `issue_refund(order_id, cents)`; an attacker embeds hidden instructions inside a support ticket.
tasks: Test multi-turn tool trajectories deterministically in CI without spending `$50` or hitting flaky live LLMs (`SHA-256` replay cassettes + mock MCP servers).
Architect defense-in-depth against **Indirect Prompt Injection** & confused-deputy tool escalation (untrusted data -> destructive tool).
Enforce JSON-Schema bounds, maximum dollar caps, human-in-the-loop (HITL) step-up auth, and `max_steps` loop breakers.
antiPatterns: auto-execute unbounded refunds from untrusted text
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Run PR trajectory tests against deterministic `SHA-256(messages + tool_schemas)` cassettes + stateful mock MCP sandboxes (paired with a small nightly live-model canary). Enforce strict JSON-Schema validation, hard policy caps in code (never prompt-only!), taint-tracking/HITL confirmation whenever untrusted ticket/email text precedes write tools, and `max_steps` loop breakers.

questions.title: Q5: LLM Inference Economics — KV-Cache Prefix Caching, PagedAttention & Quantization QA
questions.scenario: Self-hosted vLLM latency spikes (`TTFT > 3.5s`, `ITL > 90ms`) under concurrent agent traffic, and `INT4 AWQ` quantization subtly degrades JSON tool-call validity.
tasks: Calculate KV-Cache memory growth with context length and explain how **PagedAttention** + **Prefix Caching** cut `TTFT`.
Design a rigorous Quantization Regression Benchmark (`BF16` vs `FP8` vs `INT4`) measuring perplexity, RAG faithfulness, and constrained JSON/grammar accuracy.
Define streaming SSE load-test SLIs (`TTFT`, `ITL/TPOT`, `E2E latency`, token throughput) under realistic prompt-length distributions.
antiPatterns: put dynamic timestamp at the very start of system prompt breaking prefix cache
questions.benchmarkAnswer: Keep static system prompts + tool schemas byte-identical at prefix index 0 (moving timestamps/user IDs to the tail) so vLLM PagedAttention shares KV-cache blocks (`-60% TTFT`, `<4%` fragmentation). Benchmark `FP8`/`INT4` against `BF16` on hard tool-call + math/negation evals with FSM constrained decoding, and load-test SSE streams measuring `p95 TTFT` (prefill) separately from `p95 ITL/TPOT` (decode).
